reviewed: multiword plurals generated by inflecting a proper name, plus four duplicated entries
_finding: Every multiword noun_override had its plural built by mechanically inflecting each word, including the parts naming a unique place or event. That produced 'Lagi di Como', 'Monti Bianci', 'Monaci di Baviera' (Munich rendered as monks), 'Nuove Zelande', 'Champions Leagui' and 'tour di Franci', where even the French preposition de was rewritten to di. These name single entities and have no plural, so the plural is set equal to the base. The two genuine exceptions are the ones whose head really is a common noun: crociera and tendine inflect while the proper part does not. Articles are left untouched.
_dropped: farina_mandorle_noun -- byte-identical second copy of farina_di_mandorle_noun
isole_Eolie_noun -- noun_class was f_std, so its noun_override was inert and the engine derived 'isole Eoli'. The surviving isole_eolie_noun is correctly irregular and correctly capitalised.
tendine_achille_noun -- duplicate; the surviving entry is kept for its id and its rating, with the plural repaired below
ufficiale_aeronautica_noun -- duplicate; the survivor is kept because it is rated 4 rather than 7 and so is the one learners actually meet, with its articles repaired below

rows._was: tendini d'Achilli -- the name Achille was inflected
articles were la/le; ufficiale is masculine, so the app was showing 'la ufficiale dell'aeronautica'
ore i mezze -- the conjunction e was read as a plural article
